methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective review of 185 patients comparing LRA vs. PRA with 1:1 propensity score matching on sex, age, tumor laterality, BMI, tumor size, hypertension, and diabetes. Uses appropriate parametric/non-parametric tests, chi-square/Fisher's exact, and stepwise multivariate logistic regression. The PSM however identified a residual significant BMI difference (24.3 vs 25.0, p=0.013), indicating incomplete balance. Only 27 tumors >=4cm and 4 tumors >=6cm limit the generalizability to larger masses, which authors acknowledge. Surgeon selection bias (non-random assignment) and potential learning-curve confounding across four surgeons are unaddressed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Surgical comparison informs choice of retroperitoneal approach for adrenalectomy. Results concordant with Oh et al. (ref 10) and Agha et al. (ref 11). Adrenal surgery includes some oncologic indications (metastasis n=2, Cushing, pheochromocytoma) but predominantly benign disease; pathology is mostly benign adenoma (69.7%). Retrospective non-randomized cohort with PSM maps to Oxford LoE 4.

reporting_quality.justification: Appropriate standard for a comparative retrospective observational study is STROBE; not referenced. Methods describe surgical technique, trocar placement, and statistical analysis in adequate detail with ethics approval (KL901440). Clavien-Dindo classification is used for complications. No data availability statement; no sharing of code or patient-level data. Ethics approval date (10 January 2024) postdates the study period by months, which is unusual but common in retrospective analyses.

novelty_literature.justification: Authors claim this is the largest comparative analysis to date (n=185). Prior studies (Oh 2020 n<100, Agha 2008) and a network meta-analysis (Alberici 2022) already establish PRA as comparable or superior to LRA in operative time and recovery. This is an incremental single-center confirmation, with the main novelty being the PSM and logistic modeling of operative time and length of stay predictors.

writing_presentation.justification: Generally readable with a clear structure, detailed surgical technique descriptions, and informative figures of trocar placement and intraoperative views. Minor typographical issues ('gtsummray', 'hyper extended'), some redundancy, and the figure/table headers sometimes appear as unmoored descriptive paragraphs in the text. Discussion balances strengths and limitations.

key_strengths: Largest single-center LRA vs. PRA comparison to date (n=185) with all procedures by four experienced urologists using both approaches
Propensity score matching with appropriate covariate selection (sex, age, tumor laterality, BMI, size, hypertension, diabetes)
Detailed surgical technique descriptions with trocar diagrams and intraoperative photographs
Multivariate logistic regression identifying BMI, male sex, and LRA approach as independent predictors of operative time >60 min, consistent with prior literature (refs 10, 11, 24, 25)
key_concerns: Residual BMI imbalance after PSM (p=0.013) indicates incomplete adjustment and caller-to-interpret effect
Few large tumors (n=27 >=4cm, n=4 >=6cm) limits conclusions about PRA in complex cases, as authors note
No adjustment for surgeon/learning-curve effect across four operators and a five-year study period
Oncologic yield is modest (mostly benign adenoma 69.7%; only 2 metastases); applicability to adrenal malignancy is limited
Ethics approval dated 2024 for a 2018-2023 retrospective cohort is noted but not explained
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid retrospective comparative surgical outcomes study with appropriate PSM and logistic modeling but limited novelty and modest oncologic content; appropriate for a mid-tier surgical or specialty oncology journal after minor revisions.
